tweets.text:
One thing I’ve found interesting about exchange liquidity.

Volume doesn’t tell the whole story.

An exchange can have high volume without having great liquidity when you actually trade.

What matters is order book depth, active liquidity, and how much your order moves the price.

Trading costs are a good way to see this in practice.

For a $10K market order, we’re looking at the base tier taker fee plus half the effective spread.

That cost varies quite a bit across major venues. On perps, the gap is even bigger.

I also noticed on DeFiLlama that MEXC is now ranking #2 in active liquidity among all tracked exchanges, with $3.436B, behind only Binance at $4.065B.

A $10K trade on MEXC costs roughly half as much as on Binance or Bybit, for both spot and perps.

So volume is only one piece of the picture.

The more interesting question is how much usable liquidity is actually there when you need to trade, and what it costs to access it.

I looked into a lot of the coins CT has been hyping lately. These are my views after checking the actual fundamentals.

$NEAR: Intents show real usage, fee generation and buybacks. Volume is in the tens of billions cumulative with solid recent activity. Quantum-resistant signing is already optional on accounts with no migration needed. Buybacks are real, but issuance has often been higher so net supply is still expanding. Worth watching.

$ZEC: Privacy infrastructure is live and improving, with a growing shielded share of supply. Not a revenue play. More a bet on demand for financial privacy.

$TAO: Still one of the better decentralized AI setups. Subnets are generating real external revenue (recent estimates above $50M annualized) with actual customers and some revenue-funded buybacks. Emissions remain large relative to that, so I’m selective on what counts as genuine demand.

$ZRO: Strong cross-chain infrastructure with real usage. Stargate fees fund ZRO buybacks. Zero and ATLAS add an institutional settlement angle that is still mostly about what’s being built. Near-term unlock is a supply factor.

$STRK: Solid tech, real utility and growing BTCFi activity. Tokenomics remain a concern with roughly 127M STRK unlocking monthly through March 2027. Stronger demand would help absorb that supply.

$GRASS: One of the AI names actually reporting meaningful revenue. September third-party review showed about $14.5M in H1 2026. Interesting, though a material share of supply is still locked. Watching both adoption and dilution.

A few others:

$HYPE: One of the stronger business models in crypto. Real trading activity, substantial fees, and a clear mechanism sending a high share of those fees to HYPE purchases that get burned. Hard to ignore.

$MORPHO: Real adoption with genuine borrowing demand and major platform integrations. Product is finding traction, but direct token revenue capture is still limited.

$UNI: Fee switch improved the story. Established DEX usage now funds protocol-fee linked UNI burns. Better than the old governance-only setup, though burns have been modest so far.

I’m not dismissing projects just because CT is talking about them. Some have real revenue, some have good tech, and some still depend on what comes next.

There’s a difference between liking a project and paying any price for it. 
Good projects have turned into bad investments when expectations ran too far ahead of reality.

Being early to a good project and being early to a good trade are two different things.

tweets.text:
Bought some long term $SECZ exposure.

Been researching into ways to express bullishness into the tokenization sector. Fact is, there is no easy or straight forward play.

$SECZ is extremely high beta, metrics are still mediocre in terms of revenue (making a loss too), this is essentially a call option on future growth of both tokenization and Securitize itself.

Other tokenization options could include $COIN, $HOOD, $CRCL and obviously your favorite RWA/DeFi like coins. Everyone is trying to gain a small piece of the pie eventually. 

Players like Coinbase got the users and will collect a big part of it. Also with their USDC fee collection. But you're also exposed to the rest of the business, the stablecoin part is very rate sensitive and the tokenization part is really just a fraction of the exposure you're buying into at that point. As is the way for most of these plays.

Coming back to Securitize,

The 17th of September news:
The SEC opened a 5 year path for tokenized US stocks to trade onchain.

The key detail: only tokens with the same rights as the real share qualify. Dividends, voting, all of it.

That rules out most wrapper products. The other is exactly the model Securitize has been building. That gives them an edge there. Of course the market did react and price moved from ~$7 to ~$17. From which it has given back more than half of those gains by now trading back to ~$11 at the time of writing this.

The other side:
Revenue fell 5% last quarter and guidance got cut. 
Still loss making.
Supply overhang in the form of Sponsor earnout shares. This will cap rallies until that is burned through. I expect this process to take a while, even if things turn bullish.

Q3 earnings in November won't show any the SEC impact yet. So anyone betting on better guidance or metrics on November 20th will likely be disappointed.

Honestly this stock is a lot like many crypto projects. The narrative and idea is solid. But the "tokenomics" aren't the best for now. That is a obvious risk and with how volatile this moves I am mentally prepared for large daily moves and a potential further drawdown first.

So I sized it for what it is. A long dated call option. With the possibility to add in future months, possibly after the Q3 earnings.

I don't expect any metrics to magically go crazy in the next 3-6 months. This is a long term play.

I just have a high personal conviction that tokenization is going to be a big thing in the next 5+ years. 

With that in mind, it would be a waste not to express that idea in some additional way besides just my precious magic internet coins.

This is burnout, and if you want to survive as a trader, you must learn to recognize it.

True burnout is not just being overworked, nor is it something you can push through. It is a feedback loop that occurs when your body experiences intense, prolonged stress.

Stress is part of life, and under normal conditions you can recover from it easily. In fact, many dimensions of human performance - strength, endurance, mental acuity - actually require stress in order to grow.

However, growth in response to stress can only happen when the stress is manageable and offset by periods of recovery. When the stress is extreme and constant, the body fails to adapt and enters a downward spiral.

As stress accumulates, several things happen physiologically:
- sleep is disrupted
- hormones become dysregulated
- mental performance degrades
- heart rate variability falls 
- inflammation rises and immune function declines

The problem is that each of these effects also *reduces your ability to withstand and recover from stress.* So you enter a vicious cycle where recovery becomes impossible and performance steadily deteriorates.

The experience @agapestride describes here is exactly what it feels like to burn out from trading. And if you find yourself in this situation, the most important thing you can do is *recognize what has happened.* 

You are not dumber than you used to be. You are not more indecisive. You are not more impulsive, fearful, or greedy. You are simply physiologically impaired by severe, chronic stress.

When you notice the signs of burnout, you must prioritize recovery above all else:
- cut your risk
- stop looking at charts
- get off social media
- play sports or start running
- spend time with friends and family
- go hiking or traveling
- take lots of hot baths

As much as it feels like the best time to make generational wealth is RIGHT NOW, the market will always be here. So take a break and don't come back until you know your body can handle it.
